# EchoDiar

> EchoDiar is a free, open-source, local-first meeting recorder for macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows 11 (x64, Arm64) that transcribes meetings, tells speakers apart, and lets you ask AI about them.

EchoDiar is a native app on both systems: a Swift app in the Mac menu bar and a WinUI app in the Windows notification area. It records one app's audio (Zoom, Teams, Meet in a browser...) or all system audio, plus your microphone, on separate channels. Transcription runs on-device with Whisper and Parakeet on both systems (plus Qwen3-ASR and Apple Speech on macOS 26), with speaker diarization (FluidAudio on Mac, sherpa-onnx on Windows), or optionally with cloud speech-to-text services. With Whisper or Parakeet, EchoDiar transcribes while you record (the live captions come from the same model), so the transcript is ready seconds after you stop. While recording, the live transcript sits next to two tabs: Catch-up sums up what is new since the last catch-up (what happened with [mm:ss] times, what is happening now, new decisions, action items and open questions), and Chat answers questions about the meeting so far with cited times; both run on a local server, a cloud API or a CLI, and the answers are saved with the conversation. AI summaries and chat work with on-device models (MLX and Apple Foundation Models on Mac; GGUF models and Phi Silica on Copilot+ PCs on Windows), local servers (LM Studio, Ollama, Jan, llama.cpp, vLLM, plus Foundry Local on Windows), cloud APIs with your own key, or subscription CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI). On Mac, calendar triggers work with any account in macOS Calendar (iCloud, Google, Outlook/Exchange, CalDAV): when a meeting starts, EchoDiar asks, waits for the call or records right away, names the recording after the event and can stop when it ends. Screen recording (macOS only for now, opt-in per recording): a recording can also capture the entire screen, a window or a portion of the screen (turn on "Record the screen too" in the menu next to Record; Record then asks what to record, and the screen button turns the screen on and off as often as you like during a recording, with a black "Screen recording off" picture in the one video where it was off), at 15 fps by default (20, 30 or 60 optional), about 2.4 to 8.4 MB per minute for a meeting-like window depending on the quality preset, with optional cursor, click highlight, camera bubble (with optional background blur, done on the Mac) and key presses, in window recordings too; a "screen only" recording keeps screen and sound without a transcript until you transcribe it later. The video plays in sync beside the transcript (video on the left, on top or hidden), can be exported as one MP4 with both channels, the microphone, the system audio or no audio, and can be deleted by hand on Mac or by auto-delete (video only, audio and video, or the whole conversation); Windows keeps and manages these videos in its library. The screen video, the camera picture and key presses stay on the Mac; key presses are only drawn into the picture, never logged or stored, and permissions (Screen Recording, Camera, Input Monitoring) are asked only when used. Licensed AGPLv3.
